memory.note: Verified 2026-09-05 on this machine: `codex --help` lists `--add-dir <DIR>`, `-C/--cd <DIR>`, `-m`, `-a/--ask-for-approval`, `-s/--sandbox`. `--full-auto` is REJECTED by this version (`error: unexpected argument '--full-auto' found`) and was replaced here by `--ask-for-approval never --sandbox workspace-write`. Sessions live under ~/.codex/sessions partitioned by date, not by cwd, so two agents sharing a home share this state; the cwd-scoped part is the AGENTS.md the CLI reads from its working directory.

composer.note: Measured 2026-09-09 against tmux 3.4 with `tmux display-message -p -t <pane> '#{C/r:<pattern>}'`, which answers the matching line number or 0. An empty codex composer does not render a bare glyph — it renders the placeholder `› Ask Codex to do anything`. Live idle pane %385 answered 16 for this pattern and 0 for the glyph-only pattern this adapter used to ship. A pane rendering `› read the inbox` answers 0. Caveat measured at the same time: pane %448 was mid-turn (`◦ Working (50s • esc to interrupt)`) and STILL rendered the placeholder, so for codex an empty composer proves the input box is free, not that the agent is idle.

bootstrap_message: Read {{bootstrap_file}} and follow it exactly. Reply with the single word READY once you have read it and every skill it lists.
notes: Codex has no system-prompt flag in interactive mode, so the bootstrap pointer is typed as the first message. Per-agent memory is only partly cwd-scoped: AGENTS.md follows the cwd, session history does not. Set CODEX_HOME per agent in the spec's env if you need the history separated too. Coordinator form verified 2026-09-05: `codex --help` lists `-s/--sandbox <SANDBOX_MODE>` with possible value `read-only`. It is appended after auto_approve_args, so if an agent is both auto_approve and coordinates_only the read-only sandbox is the --sandbox value that survives. TM-130: the glyph-only ready pattern this adapter shipped (`^\s*[›>❯][^a-zA-Z0-9]*$`, both the JS and the tmux form) NEVER MATCHED. Re-measured 2026-09-09 against tmux 3.4 on live idle pane %385: it answered 0, while `^\s*›\s*Ask Codex to do anything` answered 16. An empty codex composer renders that placeholder, and the old pattern forbade letters after the glyph — so every codex agent burned its whole 30s timeout_ms and was then reported as a slow agent. The claim it was 'measured 2026-09-05 (a codex `› ` prompt matched)' did not survive re-measurement; it is corrected here rather than left in place. Same restrictions as every tmux-side pattern: per-line search, no `\n`, no braces, no `:`, no trailing `\s`. TM-111 still holds, by a different route: the pattern now names the placeholder text an EMPTY composer renders, so a menu row drawn with the same glyph ("❯ Yes, allow") cannot match it.
